# Plan a defect or a change request as a reviewed spec package

## Intent

A defect or a change request is a few lines of text, and nobody should
implement from that. Before any code is written, nightshift turns the text
into a spec package: a planner session writes it in a task fork of the
workspace under a package number nightshift gives, a reviewer with a fresh
context reads it against the text, and the person approves, sends back or
abandons the plan in one decision that shows the package, its draft change
on the hub and the sensitive paths it is likely to touch. An approved
package is activated on the change's branch, and the item is ready to be
implemented.

## Goals

- **Every defect and change request is carried by a spec package.** A
  planner session (`af-spec`, unattended) writes one package per item, a
  `lite` one with one requirement for a defect.
- **nightshift gives each planner its package number**, so that two
  planners at work in one workspace never take the same one.
- **A plan is accepted from the fork, not from the session's account.** The
  result file says `written`, and the package on the fork has the number
  given and validates through `afspec` with no error.
- **The plan is a draft change from the planner's first push.** The person
  reads the plan where the code will follow, and the hub never lands a
  draft.
- **A reviewer with a fresh context reviews every plan**, up to 3 rounds,
  before the person is asked.
- **The plan's approval is the one go-ahead.** A `plan` decision shows the
  package, the draft change, the files its tasks expect to touch and the
  policy rules those files would select; `approve` activates the package.
- **A person can skip the approval, not the plan.** With
  `--no-plan-approval` the item is planned and reviewed in the same way and
  goes on without a decision when the reviewer agrees.
- **Work too large for one package is not lost.** Its remaining parts
  become new, unplanned items, which wait for `nightshift item plan`.
- **An imported spec package needs no plan.** It goes from `new` straight
  to `ready`.

## Background

Packages 01 to 04 are written and none is implemented: the code this
package names of them is what their packages specify.

- **Package 03** stores an item in `new` with its kind, its title, its
  source and `plan_approval` (false when it was created with
  `--no-plan-approval`), and offers `Transition`, `Abandon`,
  `CreateLinked`, `OnChange` and `OnAbandon` of `internal/item`, and
  `RegisterKind`, `OnAnswer`, `Open` and `Append` of `internal/inbox`. An
  item made from another has the source type `item` and a `parent`. It has
  no function that changes `plan_approval` after creation.
- **Package 04** offers `Scheduler.RegisterStep(state, StepFunc)` and
  `Scheduler.RunSession(ctx, Request)`. A step function is called for each
  item in its state that is not paused and waits on no decision, one call
  at a time per item, and again after it returned. A session is described
  by a `session.Spec` (`Item`, `Role`, `Step`, `Fork`, `Branch` or
  `Commit`, `Prompt`, `Inputs`, `Accept`); in the prompt `{result}` stands
  for the path of the result file and `{input:<name>}` for the path of an
  input file. A session whose `Accept` function returns an error counts as
  failed with the first line of that error; after the second failure in a
  row for one step the item waits on `session_failed`. A reviewer's result
  carries `Verdict` with `agree` or `object` and findings (`text`, and
  `file`, `line`, `criterion` where given). From that package on,
  `command.Runner` runs every command as the session user, and the clones
  belong to that user.
- **Package 02** offers `gitclone.Sync(ctx, Options{URL, Token, Dir,
  Commit, Runner})`, which brings a clone to a commit, detached, and
  `command.Runner`.

Parley (`agent-fox-dev/parley`) is the hub. What this package uses of it,
as its `docs/api.md` states at commit `7eabfb9`:

- A **task fork** has the slug `<parent>--<name>` and copies nothing: it
  reads the parent's history, so every commit of the parent is available
  in it. With `auto_change` (the default) a push of a new branch to the
  fork opens a change by itself; with `auto_change: false` it does not.
- A **change** is opened from a branch of a fork into the parent, as a
  draft when `draft` is true. A draft may have an empty intent and never
  lands. One branch is the source of at most one draft or open change
  (`409 change_exists`, with the existing change in `details`).
- `POST …/policy/evaluate` with `paths` answers the requirements those
  paths would select, each with its `rule`, its `paths`, `approvals` (with
  `required`) and `block`, and writes nothing.
- `GET …/scm/refs/{name}` answers a ref object with the `sha` a branch
  points at, or `404 ref_not_found`.

The spec toolchain (`agent-fox-dev/spec`): `afspec` loads, validates,
renders and activates packages. PRD 09 of that repository specifies the
modes of `af-spec` this package runs (`--unattended`, `--number`,
`--no-activate`, `--defect`, `--findings`, `--result`) and the result
file. No package was generated from that PRD on 2026-11-28 and the skill
does not take these arguments yet, so nightshift's planning cannot run
against the real skill before that PRD is implemented; this package is
built and tested against a fake `claude` that behaves as PRD 09 says.

## Requirements

Constraint: Linux and macOS; Windows is best effort. Constraint: the
`nightshift` client speaks only the daemon's HTTP API.

### When planning starts

An item of kind `spec` is planned already and chosen by the person who
imported it: it goes from `new` straight to `ready`.

For a `defect` or a `change_request` created by a person (`item new`,
`item import --issue`), planning starts at once: the item goes to
`planning`. An item made from another (a part of work too large for one
package, an open item of an implementation) stays `new`, with no session
and no fork, until the person runs `nightshift item plan <N>
[--no-plan-approval]`.

`nightshift item plan <N> [--no-plan-approval]` is `POST
/api/v1/items/{number}/plan` with `{"no_plan_approval"?: bool}`. It
answers `200` with the item and the command prints `planning item <N>`.
With the option, the item's plan needs no approval, as if it had been
created with it. It is refused with `409 conflict` for an item that is not
`new` (`item 12 is ready, not new`) and for an item of kind `spec` (`item
12 is a spec package and needs no plan`), and with `404 not_found` for a
number that names no item.

### The fork, the package number and the planner

For a `defect` or a `change_request`, nightshift creates a task fork of the
workspace and starts a planner session in it. The fork is named `i<N>`
after the item's number (its slug is `<workspace>--i<N>`), is created with
`auto_change` off and the hub's default lifetime, and the item's branch in
it is `item-<N>`.

nightshift gives the planner the number of the package to write: one above
the highest package number on the default branch and above every number it
gave to an item of that workspace that is neither `done` nor `abandoned`.
The highest number on the default branch counts the directories under
`.specs/` and under `.specs/archive/` at the tip of the default branch. An
item keeps the number it was given through every round and every retry. A
number is written with two digits, three past 99.

The planner is `af-spec`, run unattended on a branch of the fork with the
item's text, the number, and the instruction to leave the package a draft
(`af-spec <text file> --unattended --number <NN> --no-activate --result
<file>`, with `--defect` for a `defect`). It writes one spec package: for a
`change_request`, a package of the profile the work needs; for a `defect`,
a `lite` package with one requirement, the behaviour as it should be. A
defect is not reproduced while planning: the failing test is written and
recorded when the package is implemented.

The item's text is the text it was created with; for an item imported from
an issue it is the issue's title, its body and its comments in order.

The session's result is accepted when its result file says `written`, and
the package on the fork has the number given and validates through
`afspec` with no finding of severity error. A result that is not accepted,
or a session that left no result file, counts as a failed session (package
04: the step is started once more, and after the second failure in a row
the item waits on `session_failed`). The reasons:

| Case | Reason |
|---|---|
| the result's `outcome` is not `written` | `planner: <outcome>: <reason>` (`planner: <outcome>` without a reason) |
| the result has no `outcome` | `planner: result has no outcome` |
| the fork has no branch `item-<N>` | `branch item-<N> is not on the fork` |
| the branch has no package directory with the number | `no package <NN> on the branch` |
| the package does not load | `package <NN> does not load: <error>` |
| the validation has an error | `package <NN> does not validate: <check>: <message>` (the first) |

When the planner reports that the work did not fit one package
(`remaining_scopes` of the result file), the package holds its first part.
Each remaining part becomes a new work item of the same kind in state
`new`, linked to the item it came from and carrying the text the planner
gave for it; like an open item of an implementation, it stays `new` until
the person runs `nightshift item plan <N>`. The `plan` decision lists them.

When the planner's branch is on the fork, nightshift opens the item's
change on the hub as a draft, with the item's title and the package's
intent (the text of the `## Intent` section of its `prd.md`).

### The review of a plan

The reviewer then reviews the package against the item's source text. It
is a session of its own (package 04) on the commit the planner pushed,
given the item's text, the package's directory and, from the second review
on, the earlier findings with the planner's replies. Its verdict is
`agree` or `object`, with findings.

On `object` the planner is started again on the draft with the findings
(`af-spec <package> --unattended --findings <file> --no-activate --result
<file>`) and revises, answering each finding; after 3 rounds without
`agree`, planning ends with the objections attached. A round is one review
and, on `object`, the revision that answers it: after the third objection
the planner revises and replies once more, and there is no fourth review.

The findings file is a JSON array; a finding has an `id`, a `source`
(`review` or `person`), a `text` and, where the reviewer named one, a
`criterion`. The planner's replies (`replies` of the result file: `id`,
`action`, `text`) are kept with the findings.

### The plan decision

Planning ends in a decision of kind `plan` in `Action`. It shows the
package's rendered text, a link to the draft change, the files its tasks
expect to touch, each policy rule those files would select that requires
an approval or blocks (`likely to need your approval under rule <name>`,
`blocked by rule <name>`), the reviewer's last verdict and, when it
objected to the end, each open finding with the planner's reply. It also
lists the items made from the parts that did not fit.

Its options are `approve`, `revise` (with a comment, required; planning
runs once more with it, the comment as a finding the planner must follow)
and `abandon`. On `approve` nightshift activates the package on the
change's branch, which freezes its requirements and tasks, and the item is
`ready`. On `abandon` the item is abandoned, as `nightshift item abandon`
does it, which abandons its change on the hub.

While the decision is open the item is `awaiting_approval`. An answer to
the decision of a paused item takes effect at the resume.

### Without a plan approval

An item created with `--no-plan-approval` is planned and its plan reviewed
in the same way, but when the reviewer agrees, no decision is opened:
nightshift activates the package, the item is `ready`, and the thread gets
the entry `plan approved at creation` with a link to the draft change.
When the reviewer objected to the end, the `plan` decision is opened all
the same. `nightshift item plan <N>` takes the same option for an item
that waits in `new`. A plan approved this way is still subject to
everything after it: the gate, the review and the hub's policy.

### The kept package text

nightshift keeps the text of every package a planner wrote in its own
store until the item is `done` or `abandoned`: every file of the package's
directory as it was on the fork when the result was accepted.

### What this package offers the later ones

- **`internal/change`**, the item's task fork and change on the hub:
  `Service.EnsureFork(ctx, item)`, `Service.OpenDraft(ctx, item, title,
  intent, sessionID)`, `Service.Head(ctx, item)` (the head of the item's
  branch on the fork), `Service.Get(ctx, item)` (a `Record` with
  `Workspace`, `Fork`, `GitURL`, `Branch`, `Generation`, `Change`,
  `ChangeRef` and `ChangeURL`), `Service.Abandon(ctx, item, reason)`,
  which is the hook registered with `item.OnAbandon`, and
  `Service.Forget(ctx, item)`, after which `EnsureFork` creates a new fork
  for the item (package 06 restores an expired fork with it).
- **`plan.Service.Reopen(ctx, item, reason, extra)`**: moves an item to
  `awaiting_approval` and has a `plan` decision opened that shows what the
  first one showed and the evidence given (package 08: the failure's
  output after a revert).
- **`plan.Service.Kept(ctx, item)`**: the last package text kept for the
  item (`Package` with `Number`, `Dir`, `Head` and `Files`).
- **`plan.Service.RegisterPrepare(name, fn)`**: a function called before
  an answer `approve` or `revise` is carried out; while it returns an
  error the answer waits (package 06 restores the fork there).
- **`plan.Service.AddFinding(ctx, item, text)`** and
  **`plan.Service.Revise(ctx, item, comment)`**: a finding of the person
  for the planner's next run, and the return of an item from
  `awaiting_approval` to `planning` (package 09: a note).
- **The decision kind `plan`** (`approve`, `revise`, `abandon`), to which
  no package adds an option.

### End-to-end flows

**A change request is planned, reviewed and approved.** The person runs
`nightshift item new demo --text "Add a greeting endpoint"`. `nightshiftd`
moves the item to `planning`, creates the task fork `demo--i1` on the hub,
takes the next package number and starts the planner; the planner pushes a
package to `item-1`; nightshift accepts it, keeps its text and opens the
draft change; the reviewer agrees; the item is `awaiting_approval` and a
`plan` decision appears in `nightshift inbox --action`. The person runs
`nightshift decide <id> --option approve`. nightshift activates the
package on the branch and the item is `ready`.

**A defect without a plan approval, sent back once, with a part split
off.** The person runs `nightshift item new demo --kind defect --text
"Greeting drops the name" --no-plan-approval`. The planner, started with
`--defect`, writes a one-requirement package and reports one remaining
scope; nightshift makes it a linked `defect` item in `new`. The reviewer
objects with one finding; the planner is started with `--findings`,
revises and replies; the reviewer agrees. No decision is opened: the
package is activated, the item is `ready` and its thread says `plan
approved at creation`. The linked item is still `new`; the person runs
`nightshift item plan <M>`, and its planner is started with the next
package number.

**A plan the reviewer objects to, sent back by the person and abandoned.**
The reviewer objects three times; after the third revision a `plan`
decision opens with the verdict `object` and each open finding with the
planner's reply. The person answers `revise` with a comment; the planner
is started with the comment as a finding of the person; the reviewer
agrees and a new `plan` decision opens. The person answers `abandon`; the
item is `abandoned` and its change is abandoned on the hub.

## Design Decisions

From the source PRD, by its numbers:

- **3. The plan's approval is the one go-ahead; an imported spec package
  needs none.** The owner decided it.
- **14. The plan is a draft change from the planner's first push.** The
  owner decided it.
- **16. nightshift gives each planner its package number.** The owner
  decided it: two planners at once would otherwise take the same one.
- **20, 21. The reviewer works in a fresh context and reviews the plan.**
  The owner decided it.
- **24. nightshift opens the change; a session's token cannot.** Chosen
  there.
- **29. Every work item is carried by a spec package, a `lite` one for a
  defect.** Kept from PRD 01.
- **31. 3 review rounds** is a starting value.
- **33. A defect is proven when it is implemented, not when it is
  planned.** The owner decided it.
- **34. A planned package is a draft until the plan is approved;
  nightshift activates it then.** The owner decided it.
- **35. The parts of work too large for one package become new, unplanned
  items, which wait for `item plan`.** The owner decided the first; the
  second is chosen there.
- **36. Every session reports through a result file.** Chosen in PRD 09 of
  `agent-fox-dev/spec`.
- **38. `--no-plan-approval` still plans and still has the plan
  reviewed.** Chosen there.

Chosen here:

1. **This package is the fifth of ten** and holds *Planning* of the source
   PRD with the item's fork and change. The owner agreed to the split on
   2026-11-28.
2. **Two Go packages: `internal/change` (the item's fork and change on the
   hub) and `internal/plan` (planning, which imports `change`).** Why:
   packages 06, 07 and 08 need the fork and the change and nothing of
   planning.
3. **Planning is driven by three step functions registered with the
   scheduler, for `new`, `planning` and `awaiting_approval`; an answer to
   a `plan` decision is stored by its handler and carried out by the step
   of `awaiting_approval`.** Why: the scheduler calls no step of a paused
   item, so an answer takes effect at the resume without further code, and
   a handler that package 03 may call twice does nothing twice.
4. **"At once" is the scheduler's next pass.** Why: the scheduler wakes on
   `item.created`, and an item created in a paused workspace must not
   start.
5. **Whether an item is planned at once is read from its source: an item
   of source type `item` waits for `item plan`, every other `defect` or
   `change_request` is planned.** Why: package 03 gives exactly the items
   made from another that source.
6. **`item plan` is `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/plan`; it is accepted for
   any `defect` or `change_request` in `new`, also one whose planning is
   due anyway, and refused with `409 conflict` otherwise.** Why: the source
   PRD names the command and no route, and gives it to "an item that waits
   in `new`".
7. **`--no-plan-approval` of `item plan` is kept with the plan, not in the
   item's `plan_approval`.** A plan needs an approval when the item's
   `plan_approval` is true and `item plan` was not run with the option.
   Why: package 03 offers no function that changes the member.
8. **The fork is named `i<N>` and the branch `item-<N>`; a fork made after
   `Forget` is `i<N>-<g>` with the generation `g` from 2.** Why: package
   04's fixtures use these names, and an expired fork may still hold its
   name when its successor is created.
9. **The fork is created with `auto_change: false`, the hub's default
   lifetime, no token and no session.** Why: nightshift opens the change
   itself, as a draft with the package's intent; the lifetime is extended
   by package 06; the session's token is minted by package 04; and the
   fork exists before its first session.
10. **A fork or a change the hub says exists already (`409 conflict`,
    `409 change_exists`) is taken as the item's.** Why: it is what a
    daemon that died between the hub's answer and its own store finds at
    the next start.
11. **The highest package number on the default branch counts the
    directories under `.specs/` and `.specs/archive/`, whether or not they
    load.** Why: `af-spec --number` refuses a number that is not above
    every one of them (PRD 09 of `agent-fox-dev/spec`).
12. **nightshift reads the fork through a clone of its own per item,
    `<clones directory>/<fork slug>.plan`, brought to a commit with
    `gitclone.Sync`.** Why: the session's clone holds what a session left
    behind, and "the package on the fork" is what the hub holds.
13. **The head of the item's branch is read with `GET …/scm/refs/{name}`
    on the fork.** Why: the planner's first push has no change yet whose
    version would name it.
14. **The planner's prompt is `/af-spec {input:text} --unattended --number
    <NN> --no-activate --result {result}` (with ` --defect`), and for a
    revision `/af-spec <package directory> --unattended --findings
    {input:findings} --no-activate --result {result}`.** Why: `specrun`
    starts a skill as a slash command, and PRD 09's own flow of a revision
    passes `--no-activate`.
15. **Planner sessions carry the step name `plan`, plan reviews
    `plan_review`.** Why: package 04 counts failures per item and step, and
    a failing reviewer is not a failing planner.
16. **The text of an imported issue is `# <title>`, the body, and each
    comment under `## Comment by <author>`.** Why: the planner takes one
    text file.
17. **The acceptance runs in the session's `Accept` function, with the
    reasons of the table under *The fork, the package number and the
    planner*.** Why: package 04 then counts a refused result as a failed
    session with that reason.
18. **A branch that already holds a valid package with the item's number
    when a first planner session would start is taken without a session.**
    Why: it is what a daemon that died after the session and before its
    own record finds; a second `af-spec --number` would refuse the number.
19. **A split part is made once per scope `name`.** Why: a revision's
    result may list the remaining scopes again.
20. **A round is one review and the revision that answers it; after the
    third objection the planner still revises, and no fourth review
    runs.** Why: the decision shows each open finding with the planner's
    reply, which exists only when the planner answered the last review.
21. **A finding's `id` is `r<round>.<n>` for the reviewer's and `p<n>` for
    the person's; a finding without a reply is shown with `no reply`.**
22. **After `revise`, the rounds are counted again from zero, and a plan
    that needs no approval goes on without a decision when the reviewer
    then agrees.** Why: "planning runs once more", and the source PRD opens
    a decision for such an item only when the reviewer objected to the
    end.
23. **A finding of the person that is pending when the reviewer agrees
    starts one more revision and review.** Why: `revise` and package 09's
    notes are the same thing to the planner, a finding it must follow.
24. **The link to the draft change is `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/
    <slug>/changes/<number>`, shown with the change's `ref`
    (`demo#3`).** Why: the hub's change object carries no URL of a page.
25. **The paths sent to `policy/evaluate` are the tasks' `touches` as they
    are written, each once, the first 2,000; with no `touches` no request
    is sent.** Why: the hub takes 1 to 2,000 paths. A requirement is shown
    as blocking when its `block` is true, else as needing an approval when
    `approvals.required` is 1 or more.
26. **`approve` is recommended when the reviewer agreed, `revise` when it
    objected to the end or an activation failed.**
27. **The package is activated by `afspec`'s `Transition`, run by
    `nightshiftd` itself in a mode `nightshiftd activate-package
    <directory>` through `command.Runner`, then committed (`chore:
    activate package <NN_name>`, author `nightshift
    <nightshift@localhost>`) and pushed to the item's branch with the
    worker token.** Why: from package 04 on the clones belong to the
    session user, for whom the daemon's user cannot write; package 04's
    helper mode is the precedent; and the push by the worker is a version
    the approver token did not create.
28. **A package that is `active` already is not activated again.** Why:
    an answer may be carried out twice, and a daemon may die between the
    push and the item's move.
29. **An activation `afspec` refuses opens a `plan` decision that carries
    the refusal; a push or a hub request that fails is tried again at the
    scheduler's next pass.** Why: the first needs the planner, the second
    ends by itself.
30. **`abandon` calls the item service's `Abandon`.** Why: one way to end
    an item, with the hooks of packages 04 and 05.
31. **Thread entries of the kinds `fork_created`, `change_opened`,
    `change_abandoned`, `plan_written`, `plan_review`, `plan_approved`
    and `activation_failed`; none marks the thread unread.** Why: the
    decision's opening marks it, through package 03.
32. **While the hub is unreachable or the worker token is not accepted,
    the steps do nothing and are called again.** Why: package 01's
    `Available`.
33. **The kept text is every regular file of the package's directory, by
    its path below the directory, with the commit it was read at; all
    kept texts of an item are removed when it becomes `done` or
    `abandoned`, with its clone.**
34. **No configuration key is added.** The 3 rounds are a parameter of the
    service with that default.
35. **A re-opened `plan` decision recommends `revise`, and is opened also
    for a plan that needed no approval.** Why: it comes back because what
    was approved did not hold (package 08: a revert), which the person
    should see before it is tried again.
36. **Functions registered with `RegisterPrepare` run before `approve` and
    `revise` are carried out, not before `abandon`.** Why: they restore a
    fork the answer needs (package 06), and an abandoned item needs none.
37. **An item moves from `new` to `planning` whether or not the hub is
    reachable; the fork, the number and the sessions wait for the hub.**
    Why: `planning` says that a plan is due, and package 04 starts no
    session without the hub.

## Glossary

- **plan**: the spec package a planner wrote for a defect or a change
  request, which the person approves before it is implemented.
- **planner, reviewer**: the roles of package 04; the planner runs
  `af-spec`, the reviewer reads the package with a fresh context.
- **package number**: the numeric prefix of a spec package's directory,
  which gives the order packages are implemented in.
- **round**: one review of a plan and, when the reviewer objects, the
  planner's revision that answers it.
- **finding**: one objection of the reviewer, or one instruction of the
  person, that the planner answers with a reply.
- **split part**: a part of the work the planner left out of the package
  because it did not fit; it becomes a linked item.
- **linked item**: an item made from another; it stays `new` until the
  person asks for its plan.
- **kept text**: the files of a package as the planner pushed them, held
  in nightshift's store until the item is `done` or `abandoned`.
- **activation**: the move of a package from `draft` to `active`, which
  freezes its intent, requirements and tasks.
- **task fork, change, draft, version, policy**: as Parley defines them
  (`docs/api.md`).
- **package, `lite`, `touches`, `active`**: as the spec format of
  `agent-fox-dev/spec` defines them.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: The item's task fork and change on the hub

**Rationale:** Every item works in a fork of its own and reaches the workspace only as one change, which nightshift opens because a session's token cannot.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a part of nightshift calls the change service's `EnsureFork(ctx, item)` for an item that has no fork stored, while the hub is available to the worker token, THE nightshiftd SHALL send `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace}/forks` with the worker token and the body `{"name": "i<N>", "auto_change": false, "purpose": "nightshift item <N>: <title>"}` (the purpose cut to 1,024 characters), store for the item the fork's slug, its git URL (the answer's `remote`), the branch name `item-<N>` and the generation 1, and append to the item's thread an entry of kind `fork_created` with the text `task fork <slug> created`, not marking the thread unread
   → returns `Record{Item, Workspace, Fork: "<workspace>--i<N>", GitURL, Branch: "item-<N>", Generation: 1, Change: 0}`; the request carries no `ttl`, `token` or `session_id`; a second call returns the stored record and sends no request; when the hub answers `409 conflict`, the fork `<workspace>--i<N>` is read with `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<workspace>--i<N>` and stored as the item's, with its `hub_url` as the git URL; `Get(ctx, item)` returns the same record, and `change.ErrNotFound` for an item with no fork
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) extended with `POST …/forks`, forks that share their parent's repository, and the workspace `demo`
   - setup: items 7 and 9 of `demo` created through internal/item over a copy of the store template
   - setup: the fixtures live in internal/change/helpers_test.go
   ```
   new file internal/change/change_test.go: rec = svc.EnsureFork(ctx, 7); assert rec == {Item: 7, Workspace: 'demo', Fork: 'demo--i7', GitURL: fakeHub's git URL of the fork, Branch: 'item-7', Generation: 1, Change: 0}; assert the one POST …/forks body == {name: 'i7', auto_change: false, purpose: 'nightshift item 7: ' + title} and bore the worker token; assert the thread's last entry == {kind: 'fork_created', text: 'task fork demo--i7 created'} and the thread is not unread; again = svc.EnsureFork(ctx, 7); assert again == rec and the fake hub saw no further request; assert svc.Get(ctx, 7) == rec; assert errors.Is(svc.Get(ctx, 8) error, change.ErrNotFound). Second case, the fake hub already holds demo--i9 and answers the POST 409 conflict: rec = svc.EnsureFork(ctx, 9); assert rec.Fork == 'demo--i9' and one GET of that workspace was sent
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN a part of nightshift calls `Forget(ctx, item)` for an item with a stored fork, and `EnsureFork` is called for the item afterwards, THE nightshiftd SHALL remove the item's stored fork and change while keeping its generation, send nothing to the hub for the forgetting, and create at that `EnsureFork` a fork named `i<N>-<g>`, g being one above the kept generation, storing it as the item's with no change
   → after `Forget`, `Get` returns `change.ErrNotFound`; the next `EnsureFork` returns a record with `Fork: "<workspace>--i<N>-2"`, `Generation: 2`, `Branch: "item-<N>"` and `Change: 0`; `Forget` for an item with no fork returns nil
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/change/change_test.go: svc.EnsureFork(ctx, 7); svc.OpenDraft(ctx, 7, 't', 'i', ''); n = fakeHub request count; assert svc.Forget(ctx, 7) == nil; assert fakeHub request count == n; assert errors.Is(svc.Get(ctx, 7) error, change.ErrNotFound); rec = svc.EnsureFork(ctx, 7); assert rec.Fork == 'demo--i7-2' and rec.Generation == 2 and rec.Change == 0 and rec.Branch == 'item-7'; forget and ensure again -> 'demo--i7-3'; assert svc.Forget(ctx, 99) == nil
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN a part of nightshift calls `Head(ctx, item)` for an item with a stored fork, THE nightshiftd SHALL request `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{fork}/scm/refs/item-<N>` with the worker token and return the commit the branch points at
   → returns the ref object's `sha`; `change.ErrNoBranch` when the hub answers `404 ref_not_found`; `change.ErrNotFound` for an item with no fork, with no request sent
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fake hub extended with `GET …/scm/refs/{name}` answering from the fork's repository
   ```
   in internal/change/change_test.go, a table over {branch item-7 pushed to the fork at commit c -> c, nil; no such branch -> '', ErrNoBranch; item 8 without a fork -> '', ErrNotFound and no request}: sha, err = svc.Head(ctx, item); assert sha and errors.Is(err, want)
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN a part of nightshift calls `OpenDraft(ctx, item, title, intent, sessionID)` for an item whose fork holds the branch `item-<N>` and that has no change stored, THE nightshiftd SHALL send `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace}/changes` with the worker token and the body `{"source": {"workspace_slug": <fork>, "branch": "item-<N>"}, "title": <title cut to 200 characters>, "intent": <intent cut to 16,000 characters>, "draft": true, "session_id": <sessionID>}` (`session_id` left out when it is empty), store the change's number and `ref` for the item, and append to the item's thread an entry of kind `change_opened` with the text `draft change <ref> opened: <url>`, not marking the thread unread
   → returns the record with `Change` the number, `ChangeRef` the hub's `ref` (`demo#3`) and `ChangeURL` `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/<workspace>/changes/<number>`; the hub holds a change in the state `draft` whose source is the fork's branch; a second call returns the stored record, sends no request and writes no entry; when the hub answers `409 change_exists`, the change `details.number` names is stored as the item's and the entry is written once
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fake hub extended with `POST …/changes` (draft changes, `409 change_exists`, `400 source_not_found`) and an accessor for a stored change
   ```
   in internal/change/change_test.go: push a commit to item-7 of demo--i7; rec = svc.OpenDraft(ctx, 7, strings.Repeat('t', 250), 'Because y', 'sess-1'); c = fakeHub.Change('demo', rec.Change); assert c.state == 'draft' and c.source == {demo--i7, item-7} and len(c.title) == 200 and c.intent == 'Because y' and c.session_id == 'sess-1'; assert rec.ChangeRef == c.ref and rec.ChangeURL == hubURL + '/api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/' + rec.Change; assert the thread's last entry == {kind: 'change_opened', text: 'draft change ' + c.ref + ' opened: ' + rec.ChangeURL}; svc.OpenDraft again -> same record, no further POST, entry count unchanged. Second case, the fake hub holds a draft change 4 for the branch and answers 409 change_exists with details {number: 4}: assert rec.Change == 4. Third case, sessionID '': assert the body has no session_id
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] WHEN an item is abandoned through the item service's `Abandon`, which calls the hook this package registers with `OnAbandon("change", …)`, or a part of nightshift calls `change.Service.Abandon(ctx, item, reason)`, THE nightshiftd SHALL send `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace}/changes/{number}/abandon` with the worker token and `{"reason": <reason>}` for the item's stored change, and append to the item's thread an entry of kind `change_abandoned` with the text `change <ref> abandoned`
   → the hub's change is `abandoned`; returns nil, with no request sent and no entry written, for an item with no fork or no change; returns nil when the hub answers `409 change_closed`; the stored record is kept
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fake hub extended with `POST …/changes/{number}/abandon`
   - setup: the change service's hook registered with the item service as daemon.Run registers it
   ```
   in internal/change/change_test.go: with a draft change stored for item 7: assert itemSvc.Abandon(ctx, 7, 'no longer wanted') == nil; assert fakeHub.Change('demo', n).state == 'abandoned' and the abandon body's reason == 'no longer wanted'; assert the thread holds {kind: 'change_abandoned', text: 'change demo#' + n + ' abandoned'}; assert svc.Get(ctx, 7).Change == n. A table over {item with a fork and no change, item with no fork, a change the fake hub answers 409 change_closed for}: assert svc.Abandon(ctx, item, 'r') == nil; for the first two assert no request was sent
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] IF `EnsureFork`, `Head`, `OpenDraft` or `Abandon` is called while `Available` of the hub client is false for the worker credential, or the hub answers one of their requests with an error other than `409 conflict` for a fork, `404 ref_not_found`, `409 change_exists` and `409 change_closed`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL return the error, store nothing and write no thread entry
   → `change.ErrHubUnavailable`, with no request sent, while the hub is not available; otherwise the hub client's typed error with the hub's status and `error_type`; the item's stored record is as it was before the call; an error of the abandon hook does not keep the item from being `abandoned` (package 03 writes it to the thread as `abandon_hook_failed`)
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/change/change_test.go, a table over {monitor unreachable -> each of the four functions returns ErrHubUnavailable and the fake hub saw no request; POST …/forks answers 429 fork_limit_reached -> EnsureFork's error has error_type 'fork_limit_reached' and Get returns ErrNotFound; POST …/changes answers 400 source_not_found -> OpenDraft's error has that type and Get(…).Change == 0; abandon answers 502 -> Abandon returns the error}: assert the entry count of the thread is unchanged. Then with the abandon answering 502: assert itemSvc.Abandon(ctx, 7, 'r') == nil and the item is 'abandoned' and its thread holds an entry of kind 'abandon_hook_failed' starting 'change: '
   ```

### REQ-2: When planning starts, and under which package number

**Rationale:** A person who typed a defect expects it planned without another command, a part split off by an agent waits until the person wants it, and two planners in one workspace must never write the same package number.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN the scheduler calls the step this package registers for the state `new` for an item of kind `spec`, THE nightshiftd SHALL move the item to `ready` through the item service's `Transition` with the reason `imported package`, creating no fork and asking for no session
   → the item is `ready`; the hub saw no request for it
   Check: unit
   - setup: a plan service over a copy of the store template with a real item service and inbox, a fake scheduler that records the sessions asked for, and the fake hub; the fixtures live in internal/plan/helpers_test.go
   ```
   new file internal/plan/start_test.go, one table over items put in 'new' {kind spec -> 'ready' with the state entry 'new -> ready: imported package'; change_request with source text -> 'planning' with 'new -> planning: planning started'; defect with source issue -> 'planning'; defect made with CreateLinked (source item) -> still 'new'; the same after svc.Request(ctx, n, false) -> 'planning'}: err = svc.StepNew(ctx, item); assert err == nil; assert itemSvc.Get(n).State == want; for every row assert the fake scheduler was asked for no session and the fake hub saw no request
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN the scheduler calls the step of the state `new` for an item of kind `defect` or `change_request` whose source type is not `item`, or for which `item plan` was run, THE nightshiftd SHALL move the item to `planning` through `Transition` with the reason `planning started`
   → the item is `planning`, so that the step of `planning` is called for it at the scheduler's next pass
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.3] WHILE an item of kind `defect` or `change_request` whose source type is `item` is `new` and `item plan` has not been run for it, THE nightshiftd SHALL leave the item in `new`: no transition, no fork, no package number, no session and no hub request
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/plan`, with no body or with `{"no_plan_approval"?: bool}`, for an item of kind `defect` or `change_request` in the state `new`, THE nightshiftd SHALL store with the item that its plan was asked for and, when `no_plan_approval` is true, that its plan needs no approval
   → status 200 with the item object of package 03; a second request for the item while it is `new` is 200 too; a `no_plan_approval` once stored as true stays true when a later request leaves it out; `plan.Service.NeedsApproval(ctx, item)` is false when the item's `plan_approval` is false or `no_plan_approval` was stored as true, and true otherwise
   Check: integration
   - setup: the route registered through the API server's Handle, the client token set
   ```
   new file internal/plan/routes_test.go, through the router, a table over a linked defect item in 'new' {no body -> 200, NeedsApproval true; {} -> 200, true; {no_plan_approval: false} -> 200, true; {no_plan_approval: true} -> 200, false; that request followed by one with no body -> 200, still false}: r = post('/api/v1/items/' + n + '/plan', body); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.number == n and r.json.state == 'new'; assert svc.NeedsApproval(ctx, n) == want. One row for an item created with no_plan_approval through POST /api/v1/items: assert NeedsApproval == false without any plan request
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/plan` names a number that is no item, an item that is not in the state `new`, or an item of kind `spec`, or carries a body that is not a JSON object, holds a member other than `no_plan_approval`, or a `no_plan_approval` that is not a boolean, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the request and store nothing
   → status 404 `not_found` with `item <N> not found`; status 409 `conflict` with `item <N> is <state>, not new` or, for a `spec` item in `new`, `item <N> is a spec package and needs no plan`; status 400 `invalid_request` for the body; the item's state and what is stored about its plan are unchanged
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/plan/routes_test.go, a table over {number 999 -> 404 not_found 'item 999 not found'; an item in 'ready' -> 409 conflict 'item 3 is ready, not new'; an item in 'planning' -> 409; a spec item kept in 'new' -> 409 'item 4 is a spec package and needs no plan'; body '[1]' -> 400; body {no_plan_approval: 'yes'} -> 400; body {x: 1} -> 400}: r = post(path, body); assert r.status, r.json.error_type and r.json.message; assert svc.NeedsApproval and the item's state are as before
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] WHEN the person runs `nightshift item plan <N>`, optionally with `--no-plan-approval` before or after the number, THE nightshiftd SHALL send `POST /api/v1/items/<N>/plan` with `{"no_plan_approval": true}` when the option is given and with `{}` otherwise, and print `planning item <N>`, or the item's JSON with `--json`
   → exit code 0 and `planning item <N>` on stdout; exit code 1 with the refusal's message on stderr when the daemon refuses; exit code 2 with the usage on stderr and no request sent when the number is missing, is not a positive integer, or a further argument follows
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test HTTP server standing in for the daemon, as the other tests of the file use
   ```
   in internal/cli/item_test.go (package 03's file), a table over {['item','plan','12'] -> POST /api/v1/items/12/plan with {} , stdout 'planning item 12\n', code 0; ['item','plan','--no-plan-approval','12'] and ['item','plan','12','--no-plan-approval'] -> body {no_plan_approval: true}; with --json -> stdout parses to the served item; the server answering 409 conflict 'item 12 is ready, not new' -> code 1, stderr 'item 12 is ready, not new\n'; ['item','plan'] , ['item','plan','x'] , ['item','plan','0'] , ['item','plan','12','13'] -> code 2, usage on stderr, the server saw no request}: code, stdout, stderr = cli.Run(args)
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any item that enters planning, give it once, and keep for it, the package number that is one above the greater of the highest numeric prefix among the directories `afspec.ListSpecDirs` lists under `.specs/` and under `.specs/archive/` at the tip of the workspace's default branch (the `head_sha` of the hub's workspace object; 0 when neither directory exists) and the highest number given to another item of the same workspace that is neither `done` nor `abandoned`
   → `plan.Service.Number(ctx, item)` returns the number as a string of two digits with a leading zero, three digits from 100 on; a second call returns the stored number without reading the branch; two items of one workspace that enter planning at the same moment get different numbers; numbers given to `done` or `abandoned` items and to items of another workspace do not count
   Check: unit
   - setup: a stub that yields the directory of the default branch's tree, in place of the hub read and gitclone.Sync
   - setup: items walked into their states with the helper of internal/item's tests or through Transition
   ```
   new file internal/plan/number_test.go, a table over a default branch tree and the numbers already given {no .specs -> '01'; .specs with 01_a and 04_b -> '05'; .specs with 03_a and archive/ with 09_old -> '10'; a directory 06_broken without prd.md -> '07'; .specs up to 04 and an item in 'planning' holding 05 -> '06'; the same with that item 'abandoned' -> '05'; with that item 'done' and its package 05 not on the branch -> '05'; .specs up to 99 -> '100'; an item of workspace 'other' holding 20 -> ignored}: n = svc.Number(ctx, item); assert n == want; assert svc.Number(ctx, item) == n with no further fetch. Then 8 items of one workspace calling Number concurrently: assert 8 distinct consecutive numbers
   ```

### REQ-3: The planner run and its result

**Rationale:** The implementer works from the package alone, so a plan counts only when the package the hub holds is the one asked for and validates.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN the scheduler calls the step this package registers for the state `planning` for an item that has no accepted package, and the item's branch on the fork holds no package with the item's number, THE nightshiftd SHALL ensure the item's fork with `change.EnsureFork`, give the item its package number, and ask the scheduler with `RunSession` for a session with the role `planner`, the step name `plan`, the fork, the branch `item-<N>`, the input `text` holding the item's text, the prompt `/af-spec {input:text} --unattended --number <NN> --no-activate --result {result}`, with ` --defect` appended for an item of kind `defect`, and the acceptance function of this requirement
   → the `session.Spec` holds exactly those values and no `Commit`, and the request no class; the input `text` is the text the item was created with, and for an item imported from an issue `# <title>`, a blank line, the body, and for each comment in order a blank line, `## Comment by <author>`, a blank line and the comment's body
   Check: unit
   - setup: the default branch of `demo` holds `.specs/01_a` to `.specs/04_d`

### REQ-4: The review rounds of a plan

**Rationale:** A plan nobody but its writer has read is the cheapest place for a mistake to hide, and a reviewer and a planner that disagree must not go on without end.

   → the `session.Spec` has no `Branch`, no `Inputs` and no `Accept`; the prompt of a plan's first review names no finding; the prompt of a later review holds each earlier finding's id and text and its reply's text, or `no reply`

### REQ-5: The plan decision

**Rationale:** The plan's approval is the person's one go-ahead, so the decision has to show what will be built, where it will land and which of their sensitive paths it is likely to touch.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN planning ended for an item whose plan needs an approval, or ended as objected for any item, THE nightshiftd SHALL move the item to `awaiting_approval` through `Transition` and, at the call of the step this package registers for that state, open one decision of the kind `plan` on the item's thread with the question `Approve the plan for item <N>?`, `item <N>` as what it blocks, and this evidence in this order: `plan` with the package's rendered text (`RenderCombined` of the package at the accepted head); `draft change` with the change's URL; `files the tasks expect to touch` with the distinct `touches` of the package's tasks in the order they first appear, one to a line, or `none`; the `policy` entries; `reviewer's verdict` with `agree` or `object`; for a plan that ended as objected one `open finding` entry for each finding of the last review, with the text `<the finding's text>`, a line break and `planner's reply: <the reply>`; and one `split off` entry for each split part with the text `item <M>: <its title>`
   → the kind `plan` is declared with the options `approve`, `revise` (comment required) and `abandon`, in that order; `approve` is recommended when the reviewer agreed and `revise` when it objected to the end; a plan that ended as agreed has no `open finding` entry; exactly one `plan` decision is open for the item however often the step is called; the item's `waiting_on` names it
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real inbox with the kind `plan` declared by the plan service's registration, as daemon.Run does it
   - setup: the fake hub's `policy/evaluate` answering no requirement that needs an approval or blocks

### REQ-6: Plans without an approval, re-opened decisions and continuity

**Rationale:** A small fix should not wait for a person who already said go, a plan whose landing was reverted comes back to the same decision, and none of this may be lost or doubled by a restart or a hub outage.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN planning ended as agreed for an item whose plan needs no approval: the item was created with `--no-plan-approval`, or `item plan` was run for it with that option, THE nightshiftd SHALL activate the package on the change's branch as an approval does, open no decision, append to the item's thread an entry of kind `plan_approved` with the text `plan approved at creation: <the change's URL>`, and move the item from `planning` to `ready` with the reason `plan approved at creation`
   → the item is `ready` and was never `awaiting_approval`; no `plan` decision exists for it; the package on the fork's branch is `active`
   Check: integration
   - setup: the scripted sessions and the fake hub of the acceptance checks, with a real command.Runner and the re-executed test binary for the activation
   ```

   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHEN planning ended as objected for an item whose plan needs no approval, THE nightshiftd SHALL open the `plan` decision all the same, as for an item whose plan needs an approval

   Check: same as REQ-6.1

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A change request is planned, reviewed and approved

1. **person** runs `nightshift item new demo --text "Add a greeting endpoint"`
2. **nightshiftd** moves the item from `new` to `planning`, creates the task fork `demo--i1` on the hub, gives the item the package number `02` and starts a planner session with `--number 02`
3. **hub** creates the fork and serves it to git
4. **planner** writes `.specs/02_greeting` on `item-1`, pushes the branch and writes the result file with `outcome: written`
5. **nightshiftd** reads the branch's head from the hub, validates the package in a clone of its own, keeps its text, opens the draft change with the item's title and the package's intent, and starts a reviewer session on that commit
6. **reviewer** reads the package and answers with the verdict `agree`
7. **nightshiftd** asks the hub which rules the tasks' `touches` would select, moves the item to `awaiting_approval` and opens the `plan` decision
8. **person** reads the decision in `nightshift inbox --action` and runs `nightshift decide <id> --option approve`
9. **nightshiftd** activates the package in its clone, pushes the commit to `item-1` and moves the item to `ready`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with its scheduler, session service, inbox, item service, change service, plan service and store on disk, the nightshift client's run function, git, against the fake hub's git endpoint, afspec, for the validation, the render and the activation, the `activate-package` mode of the binary, started as a process through command.Runner

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub (internal/hubtest) with the workspace `demo` registered through the end-to-end helper of package 02, its default branch holding `.specs/01_a`
- the three roles configured, `sessions.unisolated = true`, the helper and `activate-package` being the test binary re-executed
- a fake `claude` executable on PATH, a script the test writes: it reads its prompt, and for a prompt with `--number` writes the fixture package under that number into `.specs/`, for one with `--findings` reads the findings file and changes the package's `prd.md`, commits, pushes the checked-out branch and writes the result file the prompt names (`outcome: written`, and what the test scripts as `remaining_scopes` and `replies`)
- the fake hub's policy has a rule `deploy` that requires one approval for `deploy/**`; the fixture package's tasks touch `deploy/config.yaml` and `api/greet.go`
- the reviewer's provider/faux client answers `{"verdict":"agree","findings":[]}`

**End state:**

- the fake hub holds the fork `demo--i1` and one change from its branch `item-1`, opened as a draft with the item's title and the fixture's intent
- `nightshift decision show <id>` prints the kind `plan`, the options `approve`, `revise` and `abandon`, the rendered package, the change's URL, both touched files, `likely to need your approval under rule deploy` and the verdict `agree`
- after the answer `nightshift item show 1` prints `state: ready`, and the package at the head of `item-1` on the fake hub has the status `active`
- the item's thread lists entries of the kinds `fork_created`, `plan_written`, `change_opened`, `plan_review` and `plan_approved`

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, with the startDaemon helper of package 01: d = startDaemon(cfg); assert cli(['item','new','demo','--text','Add a greeting endpoint']).code == 0; eventually cli(['inbox','--action']) names a plan decision; id = its id; out = cli(['decision','show', id]); assert out contains 'likely to need your approval under rule deploy', 'deploy/config.yaml', 'api/greet.go' and 'agree'; c = fakeHub.Changes('demo')[0]; assert c.source == {demo--i1, item-1} and c.intent == the fixture's intent; assert cli(['decide', id, '--option', 'approve']).code == 0; eventually cli(['item','show','1']) contains 'state: ready'; s = afspec.LoadSpec(checkout of fakeHub.Ref('demo--i1','item-1') + '/.specs/02_greeting'); assert s.Status == 'active'; assert the kinds of the thread's entries hold the five named
```

### PATH-2: A defect without a plan approval is sent back once and splits off a part

1. **person** runs `nightshift item new demo --kind defect --text "Greeting drops the name" --no-plan-approval`
2. **nightshiftd** creates the fork, gives the package number and starts the planner with `--number <NN> --defect`
3. **planner** writes a one-requirement package, pushes it and reports one remaining scope in its result file
4. **nightshiftd** accepts the package, makes the remaining scope a linked `defect` item in `new`, opens the draft change and starts the reviewer
5. **reviewer** answers `object` with one finding
6. **nightshiftd** starts the planner again with `--findings` and the finding as `r1.1`
7. **planner** revises the package, pushes it and replies to the finding
8. **reviewer** answers `agree` on the revised package
9. **nightshiftd** opens no decision: activates the package, writes `plan approved at creation` to the thread and moves the item to `ready`
10. **person** runs `nightshift item plan <M>` for the linked item
11. **nightshift** sends `POST /api/v1/items/<M>/plan` and prints `planning item <M>`
12. **nightshiftd** moves the linked item to `planning` and starts its planner with the next package number

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with its scheduler, session service, inbox, item service, change service, plan service and store on disk, the nightshift client's run function, git, against the fake hub's git endpoint, afspec and the `activate-package` mode of the binary

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub (internal/hubtest) with the workspace `demo` registered through the end-to-end helper of package 02, its default branch holding `.specs/01_a`
- the three roles configured, `sessions.unisolated = true`, the helper and `activate-package` being the test binary re-executed
- a fake `claude` executable on PATH, a script the test writes: it reads its prompt, and for a prompt with `--number` writes the fixture package under that number into `.specs/`, for one with `--findings` reads the findings file and changes the package's `prd.md`, commits, pushes the checked-out branch and writes the result file the prompt names (`outcome: written`, and what the test scripts as `remaining_scopes` and `replies`)
- the fake `claude` reports `remaining_scopes: [{name: "audit_log", summary: "…", text: "Log every greeting"}]` in its first result and `replies: [{id: "r1.1", action: "changed", text: "…"}]` in its second
- the reviewer's provider/faux client answers `object` with one finding, then `agree`

**End state:**

- the first `claude` invocation's prompt ends `--defect` and holds `--number 02`; the second holds `--findings` and its findings file holds the finding with the id `r1.1`
- item 1 is `ready`, no decision was ever opened for it, and its thread holds the entry `plan approved at creation: <the change's URL>`
- the package at the head of `item-1` has the status `active`
- item 2 exists as a `defect` with the parent 1 and stayed `new` until `nightshift item plan 2`, which exits 0 and prints `planning item 2`
- afterwards the fake hub holds the fork `demo--i2` and a `claude` invocation for item 2 holds `--number 03`

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: d = startDaemon(cfg); cli(['item','new','demo','--kind','defect','--text','Greeting drops the name','--no-plan-approval']); eventually cli(['item','show','1']) contains 'state: ready'; assert the recorded claude prompts: [0] contains '--number 02' and ends '--defect', [1] contains '--findings'; assert the recorded findings file == [{id: 'r1.1', source: 'review', text: …}]; assert cli(['inbox','--action']) lists no decision and GET /api/v1/decisions?state=all holds none of item 1; assert cli(['thread','show', t1]) contains 'plan approved at creation: '; assert cli(['item','show','2']) contains 'state: new' and fakeHub has no fork demo--i2; code, out = cli(['item','plan','2']); assert code == 0 and out == 'planning item 2\n'; eventually fakeHub has the fork demo--i2 and a recorded claude prompt contains '--number 03'
```

### PATH-3: A plan the reviewer objects to is sent back by the person and then abandoned

1. **person** runs `nightshift item new demo --text "Rework the greeting"`
2. **planner** writes the package and, after each objection, a revision with its replies
3. **reviewer** answers `object` three times
4. **nightshiftd** ends planning after the third revision, with no fourth review, and opens the `plan` decision with the verdict `object` and each open finding with the planner's reply
5. **person** runs `nightshift decide <id> --option revise --comment "Use the existing router"`
6. **nightshiftd** moves the item back to `planning` and starts the planner with the comment as the finding `p1` of the person
7. **reviewer** answers `agree` on the revised package
8. **nightshiftd** opens a new `plan` decision
9. **person** runs `nightshift decide <id> --option abandon`
10. **nightshiftd** abandons the item, which asks the hub to abandon its change, and removes the kept package texts
11. **hub** marks the change `abandoned`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with its scheduler, session service, inbox, item service, change service, plan service and store on disk, the nightshift client's run function, git, against the fake hub's git endpoint, afspec

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub (internal/hubtest) with the workspace `demo` registered through the end-to-end helper of package 02, its default branch holding `.specs/01_a`
- the three roles configured, `sessions.unisolated = true`, the helper and `activate-package` being the test binary re-executed
- a fake `claude` executable on PATH, a script the test writes: it reads its prompt, and for a prompt with `--number` writes the fixture package under that number into `.specs/`, for one with `--findings` reads the findings file and changes the package's `prd.md`, commits, pushes the checked-out branch and writes the result file the prompt names (`outcome: written`, and what the test scripts as `remaining_scopes` and `replies`)
- the reviewer's provider/faux client answers `object` with one finding three times, then `agree`
- the fake `claude` replies to every finding of a findings file

**End state:**

- the fake hub recorded exactly 3 reviewer sessions and 4 planner sessions before the first decision opened
- `nightshift decision show` of the first decision prints the verdict `object` and one `open finding` with `planner's reply:`
- `nightshift decide <id> --option revise` without `--comment` exits 1 with the daemon's `comment_required` message
- the findings file of the planner session after the answer holds exactly `{id: p1, source: person, text: Use the existing router}`
- a second `plan` decision opens with the verdict `agree`
- after `abandon`, `nightshift item show 1` prints `state: abandoned` and the fake hub's change is `abandoned`

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: d = startDaemon(cfg); cli(['item','new','demo','--text','Rework the greeting']); eventually a plan decision is open; id1 = its id; assert the fake hub's sessions by archetype == {planner: 4, reviewer: 3}; out = cli(['decision','show', id1]); assert out contains 'object' and "planner's reply:"; assert cli(['decide', id1, '--option', 'revise']).code == 1; assert cli(['decide', id1, '--option', 'revise', '--comment', 'Use the existing router']).code == 0; eventually a second plan decision id2 is open; assert the recorded findings file of the fifth claude invocation == [{id: 'p1', source: 'person', text: 'Use the existing router'}]; assert cli(['decision','show', id2]) contains 'agree'; assert cli(['decide', id2, '--option', 'abandon']).code == 0; eventually cli(['item','show','1']) contains 'state: abandoned'; assert fakeHub.Changes('demo')[0].state == 'abandoned'
```

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `go vet ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/change/... ./internal/plan/... ./internal/hub/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/daemon/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `01` — uses the hub client with Available and its typed error, the fake hub, the API server's Handle, the client's Register, the store's migrations and the e2e helper
- `02` — uses command.Runner, gitclone.Sync, the clones directory and the hub client's Workspace
- `03` — moves items with Transition, Abandon and CreateLinked, registers with OnChange and OnAbandon, and declares the decision kind `plan` in the inbox's registry
- `04` — registers its step functions with the scheduler and runs planner and reviewer sessions through RunSession

## Tasks

### 1. Create the item's task fork, open its draft change and abandon it (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Extend internal/hubtest: `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/forks` (the name's format, `409 conflict` for a name the parent has, a scriptable error, the fork sharing its parent's repository and served at a git endpoint of its own, reusing what package 04 added for a seeded fork), `GET …/scm/refs/{name}` answering from the repository with `404 ref_not_found`, `POST …/changes` (draft changes, `400 source_not_found` for a branch the fork lacks, `409 change_exists` with details), `POST …/changes/{number}/abandon` (`409 change_closed`), and accessors Fork, Ref, Change and Changes for tests
- 1.2 Add the change behaviours to internal/change/change_test.go and confirm they fail; keep the fixtures (a change service over a copy of the store template of internal/store with a real item service and inbox, the fake hub with the workspace `demo`) in internal/change/helpers_test.go, the one helpers file of the package
- 1.3 Add to the hub client of internal/hub, each sent with the worker credential and returning Parley's error envelope as the typed error package 01 defines: CreateFork(ctx, parent, name, purpose) sending auto_change false, Ref(ctx, slug, name), OpenChange(ctx, slug, request) and AbandonChange(ctx, slug, number, reason); cover the request bodies in internal/hub/client_test.go
- 1.4 Add internal/change with a store migration registered with internal/store: per item the workspace, the generation, and for the current generation the fork's slug, its git URL, the branch, the change's number and its ref; construct the service with change.New over the store, the hub client, the item service and the inbox, with no package-level state
- 1.5 Add EnsureFork: return the stored record without a request; otherwise refuse with ErrHubUnavailable while Available of the worker credential is false, create the fork `i<N>` (or `i<N>-<g>` from generation 2 on) with the purpose `nightshift item <N>: <title>` cut to 1,024 characters, take a `409 conflict` as the item's own fork by reading its workspace object with the hub client's Workspace, store the record and write the `fork_created` entry through the inbox's Append without the unread mark
- 1.6 Add Get (ErrNotFound for an item with no fork), Head (the branch's sha, ErrNoBranch for `404 ref_not_found`) and Forget (drop the fork and the change of the current generation, keep the generation, send nothing)
- 1.7 Add OpenDraft: return the stored record when the item has a change; otherwise open the change as a draft from the fork's branch into the workspace with the title cut to 200 characters, the intent cut to 16,000 and the session id where one is given, take a `409 change_exists` as the item's own change from its details, store the number and the ref, build ChangeURL from the hub's endpoint, and write the `change_opened` entry
- 1.8 Add Abandon: nothing to do and nil for an item with no fork or no change; otherwise abandon the change with the reason, treat `409 change_closed` as done, and write the `change_abandoned` entry
- 1.9 Return the hub client's error unchanged from all four for any other answer, store nothing and write no entry in that case
- 1.10 Create the change service in daemon.Run after the item service and register its Abandon with the item service's OnAbandon under the name `change`, after the hook of package 04, so that an item's sessions are ended before its change is abandoned; hand the service to the end-to-end helper of internal/daemon/e2e_test.go
- 1.11 Name the fake hub's fork, ref and change routes under Repository Specifics in .specs/steering.md, and add internal/change to docs/architecture.md with what later packages call: EnsureFork, OpenDraft, Head, Get, Abandon, Forget and the names of the fork and the branch

### 3. Run the planner, accept its package from the fork and keep its text (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the planner behaviours to internal/plan/planner_test.go and the acceptance behaviours to internal/plan/accept_test.go and confirm they fail; build the fixture packages through afspec itself (CreateSpec, the artefacts filled, Save) once per test process and copy them per test: a valid draft `greeting`, one with a validation warning, one whose task names an unknown criterion, one without a `## Intent` section; let the fake scheduler run a scripted function as the session, which may push to the fake hub's fork, calls the Spec's Accept with the scripted result, and returns `completed`, or `failed` with the first line of Accept's error
- 3.2 Add StepPlanning, the step function of the state `planning`, and register it with Scheduler.RegisterStep; it does one thing per call and returns, so that the scheduler calls it again: ensure the fork, give the number, then act on the plan's phase; the phase of a new plan is `draft`
- 3.3 At the phase `draft`, first look at the fork: when Head finds the branch and the package with the item's number is there and passes the acceptance, take it as accepted without a session; otherwise ask RunSession for the planner session with the step name `plan`, the branch `item-<N>`, the input `text` and the prompt with `--number`, ` --defect` for a defect, and no class
- 3.4 Build the item's text from its source: the stored text, or for an issue the title, the body and each comment under `## Comment by <author>`
- 3.5 Add the acceptance function given as the Spec's Accept: parse the result document, refuse a missing outcome and any outcome but `written` with its reason, read the branch's head with the change service's Head, bring the `.plan` clone to it with gitclone.Sync, find the directory under `.specs` whose prefix equals the number as a number, load it with afspec.LoadSpec and validate it with ValidateInRoot over `.specs` of the clone; return the reasons of the criterion as errors and ignore warnings
- 3.6 After a `completed` result, in one store transaction: record the directory, the head and the phase `review`, and store the kept text, every regular file under the package's directory read from the clone, with the number, the directory and the head; then write the `plan_written` entry
- 3.7 Create the split parts from `remaining_scopes` of the result with the item service's CreateLinked, in the order listed, of the item's kind, with the scope's text or its summary, skipping a name the plan already holds, and record each new item's number with the name
- 3.8 Open the draft change with the change service's OpenDraft when the item has none: the item's title, the `## Intent` section of the package's PRD body without its heading, and the session's id (empty for a package taken without a session)
- 3.9 Return from the step without changing the plan for a result that is not `completed` and for sched.ErrNotStarted, and return the context's error for a cancelled context
- 3.10 Add Kept(ctx, item), returning the text stored last or ErrNotFound, and register with the item service's OnChange a hook that, when an item becomes `done` or `abandoned`, deletes every kept text and the plan's clone directory `<clones directory>/<fork slug>.plan`, the latter through the Runner so that it works for a clone the session user owns
- 3.11 Add to docs/architecture.md the planner's prompt, the acceptance order with its reasons, the kept text with Kept, and the clone nightshift reads the fork through

### 4. Have every plan reviewed, for up to three rounds (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the review behaviours to internal/plan/review_test.go and confirm they fail
- 4.2 At the phase `review`, ask RunSession for a reviewer session with the step name `plan_review`, the fork and the accepted head as the commit; build its prompt, the review brief, from the item's text, the package's directory, the verdict object package 04 requires (`{"verdict": "agree" | "object", "findings": [{"text", "file"?, "line"?, "criterion"?}]}`) and, where the plan has findings of earlier reviews, each with its id, its text and its reply; give it no inputs and no Accept
- 4.3 On the verdict `agree`: add one to the round, store the verdict and write the `plan_review` entry `reviewer: agree`; with no pending finding of the person set the phase `ended`, otherwise set the phase `revise` with no reviewer finding
- 4.4 On the verdict `object`: add one to the round, replace the plan's findings by the verdict's with the ids `r<round>.<n>`, store the verdict, write the entry `reviewer: object, <n> findings` and set the phase `revise`
- 4.5 At the phase `revise`, ask for a planner session with the step name `plan`, the branch, the input `findings` (the JSON array: the plan's reviewer findings as `{id, source: "review", text, criterion?}`, then the pending findings of the person as `{id, source: "person", text}`) and the prompt with `--findings` and the package's directory, with the acceptance function of the planner run
- 4.6 After a `completed` revision: keep the text as after a first result, store each reply of `replies` with the finding of its id and `no reply` for a finding without one, mark the findings of the person it carried as delivered, create split parts for scope names not seen before, and set the phase `review`, or `ended` when the verdict is `object` and the round has reached the number of rounds
- 4.7 Add AddFinding(ctx, item, text) with its refusals ErrInvalid and ErrNotPlanning; a finding of the person gets the next id `p<n>` of the item and stays pending until a revision carried it
- 4.8 Describe the rounds, the findings file, the ids and AddFinding in docs/architecture.md

- 5.3 At the phase `ended` in StepPlanning, for a plan that needs an approval or whose verdict is `object`, move the item to `awaiting_approval` with the reason `plan ready for approval`
